name: Silas
bio: Silas, a leading man among the Jerusalem brethren and a prophet, was chosen along with Judas Barsabas to carry the Jerusalem Council's letter to the Gentile believers in Antioch, encouraging them that they need not be circumcised but should abstain from food offered to idols, blood, meat from strangled animals, and sexual immorality; afterward he chose to remain in Antioch. When Paul and Barnabas later split over whether to bring John Mark on their next journey, Paul chose Silas as his companion instead, and the two departed for Syria and Cilicia (Acts 15:22-41). His further travels with Paul are told in the chapters ahead. Silas accompanied Paul to Philippi, where he too was seized, beaten, and imprisoned after Paul exorcised a slave girl's masters' source of profit; at midnight Silas joined Paul in praying and singing praises to God, and after the earthquake opened the prison, he too was released the next day once the magistrates learned they were Roman citizens (Acts 16:19-40). Silas remained with Paul through Thessalonica and Berea, but stayed behind in Berea with Timothy when Paul went on to Athens (Acts 17:1-15). Silas rejoined Paul in Corinth, arriving from Macedonia with Timothy (Acts 18:5). He is also called Silvanus in several of Paul's and Peter's later letters. Peter later wrote his first epistle through Silvanus (Silas), describing him as a faithful brother (1 Peter 5:12).
